0007_identity_same_user_fks.constraint-scan: identity.users is created one migration earlier and has never held a row in any environment: the platform is pre-launch, so validating these composite foreign keys scans nothing and blocks nobody. A same-user foreign key added to a populated users has to go in NOT VALID and be validated by a second migration.

0013_identity_four_eyes.constraint-scan: identity.admin_action_approvals and identity.admin_role_assignments are created in 0008 and are empty in every environment: the platform is pre-launch, so validating these four-eyes CHECKs scans no rows and takes its ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock against no reader.

0015_identity_desc_indexes.drop-index-lock: identity.identity_audit_log and identity.users are empty in every environment: the platform is pre-launch. Once they are not, these two tables are the ones that will be largest, and dropping an index on either has to happen outside the migrator - drizzle runs every migration in one transaction and Postgres refuses CONCURRENTLY there.
0015_identity_desc_indexes.index-lock: identity.identity_audit_log and identity.users are empty in every environment: the platform is pre-launch, so each of these four indexes is built over zero rows. The same rebuild on a live append-only audit log would block every insert for the length of the whole migration run and belongs in an operations step instead.

0025_trade_accepted_terms_fk.constraint-scan: trade.trades and trade.trade_terms_versions are created four migrations earlier in the same chain and have never held a row in any environment: the platform is pre-launch, so validating these two composite foreign keys scans nothing and blocks nobody. Added to a populated trades, a same-trade foreign key has to go in NOT VALID and be validated by a second migration — and the terms version a trade points at is the only record of what was agreed, so it is worth the second migration rather than a long lock.

0043_ledger_fee_liability_account.constraint-scan: ledger.ledger_accounts is empty in every environment: the platform is pre-launch and the ledger has never held a posting, so re-adding ledger_accounts_scope validates zero rows. The CHECK is total over the account type enum and is what stops one kind of money being written into two different accounts, so it cannot ship NOT VALID and be validated later — an unvalidated scope rule is the same as no scope rule for the rows written in between.
0043_ledger_fee_liability_account.drop-object: Both drops are the cost T-070's status note priced in for adding an account type: account_key is GENERATED ALWAYS from a CASE over ledger_account_type and ALTER COLUMN ... SET EXPRESSION is PG 18, so the column is dropped and re-added with the new expression in this same transaction, and the renamed-away enum type is dropped once nothing references it. No reader loses anything: account_key exists again before the transaction commits, with the same name, type and unique index, and the ledger has no production data.
0043_ledger_fee_liability_account.index-lock: ledger_accounts_key_unique is rebuilt, not added: dropping the generated account_key column drops it, and this statement puts it back over the same zero rows. ledger.ledger_accounts is empty in every environment and the platform is pre-launch. On a populated ledger this whole migration belongs in a maintenance window, because the column drop itself already takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE for a full rewrite.
0043_ledger_fee_liability_account.not-null-no-default: account_key is a GENERATED ALWAYS ... STORED column, so Postgres computes a value for every existing row as part of the same ADD COLUMN and NOT NULL can never fail on it — a DEFAULT is not merely unnecessary, it is rejected on a generated column. The rule's failure mode does not apply.
0043_ledger_fee_liability_account.rename: The enum type is renamed only so a new one can take its name in the same transaction, and is dropped before that transaction commits; no release ever observes the old name. The rebuild is forced: ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE cannot be used in the transaction that adds it, and the drizzle migrator runs every pending migration in one transaction, so extending ledger_account_type in place does not run at all.
0043_ledger_fee_liability_account.type-change: ledger_accounts.account_type is retyped from the old ledger_account_type to the rebuilt one, which has the same labels plus BUYER_PROTECTION_FEE_LIABILITY: nothing narrows and no existing value can fail to fit. The rewrite is over zero rows — ledger.ledger_accounts is empty in every environment and the platform is pre-launch.
